forces.title: Union Health Ministry proposes reclassification of 16 drugs to OTC category
forces.description: The Union health ministry has issued a draft notification proposing the reclassification of 16 drugs, including common medications like paracetamol 500 mg, certain laxatives, nasal decongestants, and topical antifungal creams, into the Over-The-Counter (OTC) drug category. This regulatory change aims to enhance accessibility for consumers, allowing them to purchase these essential medicines without a prescription, thereby significantly boosting the self-medication segment and promoting public health convenience.

forces.title: Increasing consumer propensity for self-medication boosts OTC market
forces.description: Indian consumers are exhibiting a growing inclination towards self-medication, a behavioral shift that is expected to significantly boost the Over-The-Counter (OTC) drug market. This trend is driven by factors such as increasing health awareness, a desire for convenience, and the ability to manage minor health issues independently. This rising propensity directly translates into higher demand for branded OTC medicines and self-care products, providing a strong tailwind for the sector.

forces.title: Uniform 5% GST on most medicines enhances affordability
forces.description: The implementation of a uniform 5% GST on the majority of drugs and medicines, alongside nil rates for critical life-saving therapies, is a significant positive development. This policy aims to reduce patient costs, directly enhancing the affordability and accessibility of Over-The-Counter (OTC) medicines. By ensuring input tax credits are preserved, the policy avoids upstream cost build-up, allowing cost benefits to be passed to consumers, thereby stimulating demand and fostering growth in the self-medication market.

viewpoints.title: India's OTC drug market projected to nearly double by 2030
viewpoints.description: An EY report, published on January 27, 2026, projects a significant positive outlook for India's Over-The-Counter (OTC) drug market. It is expected to grow from approximately INR 47,000 crore (US$ 5.68 billion) in 2024 to INR 98,000 crore (US$ 10.38 billion) by 2030. This robust expansion is primarily driven by the increasing demand for self-care products and a broader consumer trend towards wellness, underscoring the sector's strong growth trajectory.
